Figure 1:A correct result is only part of what a teacher demonstrates.AutoMaster designs natural-language skills to guide teacher rollouts
and selects demonstrations for fine-tuning.(a)In this example, both pipelines process all 100 records with four workers. The skill-guided teacher also checks whether the fix holds with fewer or more workers.(b)With the same teacher, task pool, training set size,
and SFT recipe, students trained with AutoMaster achieve higher
performance than their Vanilla SFT counterparts on all three
benchmarks at both model sizes (4B and 9B).
Labels above the bars show gains of 1.42–8.99 percentage points
over Vanilla SFT. Error bars show±\pm1 SD over three evaluation
runs per checkpoint.

Figure 2:Overview of AutoMaster.An LLM agent designs skills for subsets of a fixed training task pool and tests them in pilot teacher rollouts. It refines the skills as needed, runs promising interventions on larger batches, and selects demonstrations for SFT. In each outer-loop round, the student is trained from the same initial checkpoint, with any skill instructions used by the teacher retained in the training input. The student is evaluated without generated skills.

Figure 3:Infrastructure of AutoMaster.The agent accesses data and submits rollout and SFT jobs through the MCP
interface. After SFT, the execution controller automatically schedules
evaluation on a separate GPU cluster, where SGLang workers load the
checkpoint directly from storage shared with the training cluster.
Linked experiment records let the agent trace each evaluation back to
the training set and the skills that guided the teacher.

Figure 5:Skill-guided changes in teacher behavior.Each column compares unguided and skill-guided rollouts by the same
teacher on the same task.(a) Terminal:Both solvers meet the error threshold. The unguided teacher claims
fourth-order accuracy despite evidence of second-order convergence.
The skill-guided teacher switches to a nine-point stencil and verifies fourth-order convergence using direct solves on successively finer grids.(b) Search:Both rollouts identify the same episode. The unguided teacher repeatedly
guesses the award, while the skill-guided teacher identifies the director
from episode credits and verifies the clues.(c) SWE:The unguided teacher reverses the global sort to satisfy a flawed self-test. The skill-guided teacher checks the UTF-16 encoding, corrects the self-test input, and keeps the required ascending order.

Figure 7:Explicit use of skill context in teacher demonstrations.Two examples from the SFT corpus illustrate how skill instructions
inform the teacher’s reasoning and actions.(a)The teacher applies a conditional rule to distinguish interpreter
invocation from direct execution, avoiding an unnecessary permission change.(b)The teacher references the supplied grammar to derive an expression’s
grouping, then implements and tests the corresponding parser.
Skill instructions and trajectory excerpts are condensed.
Quotation marks indicate verbatim excerpts.
